name: Colony of New South Wales
alt: Crown colony of New South Wales

successors.name: Commonwealth of Australia
successors.text: New South Wales, which on 1 January 1901 'became a state' of the Commonwealth; the ACT and Jervis Bay were cut from it in 1911 and 1915

ledger.x: 1788: Governor Phillip proclaims the Colony of New South Wales, all of eastern Australia east of 135 E.
1810: Macquarie Island is claimed for the United Kingdom and declared part of New South Wales (11 July 1810); one grid cell.
1825: the colony is extended west to 129 E.
1825: Van Diemen's Land becomes a separate colony.
1836: South Australia is cut from the colony.
1844: Norfolk Island is transferred to Van Diemen's Land (26 September 1844); no grid cell.
1851: Victoria is cut from the colony.
1859: Queensland is cut from the colony.
1861: the land west of South Australia passes to South Australia.

1862: the land east of 138 E north of South Australia passes to Queensland (13 March 1862): 'Land north of South Australia and east of 138 degrees east was transferred to Queensland'; the Queensland page: 'Queensland's western boundary changed from longitude 141 E to 138 E'.
1863: the Northern Territory passes to South Australia (6 July 1863): 'The New South Wales region north of South Australia was transferred to South Australia' (the Northern Territory).
1880: Macquarie Island becomes part of Tasmania (17 June 1880); one grid cell.

wars.name: Hawkesbury and Nepean wars
wars.outcome: The page: 'The first frontier war began in 1795 when encroaching British settlers established farms along the Hawkesbury River' and it 'ended the conflict by killing 14 Indigenous Australians in an ambush on their campsite' in 1816.

wars.name: Bathurst War
wars.outcome: 'Governor Brisbane proclaimed martial law on 14 August 1824' in response to fighting with Wiradjuri warriors; no border changed.

certainty.note: Every colonial border here is a line in letters patent or an act (meridians 129, 132, 135, 138 and 141 E, the 26 S parallel, the Murray River), dated in the Territorial evolution of Australia page, so the lines are drawn sharp.
